learning_outcomes.text: Students independently develop a startup idea.
They design and evaluate suitable business models.
They assess the potential economic success of the business model (viability test).
Students can inspire others with their ideas and use an Elevator Pitch for this purpose.
They are familiar with the essential elements of financial planning (capital requirements, liquidity, profitability).
They can carry out concrete financial planning with Microsoft® Excel®.
They select suitable financing sources and can access them.
Students choose a suitable legal form and create a convincing business plan for their startup.
They actively manage their founding risk.

syllabus_topics: Entrepreneurial thinking and developing business ideas (Effectuation)
Designing and evaluating business models (Business Model Canvas)
Viability testing and Elevator Pitch (with video feedback)
Understanding corporate finance (capital requirements, liquidity, profitability)
Planning and controlling finances (with Microsoft® Excel®)
Financial planning: Questions and answers (input and sales tax, loss carryforwards and income taxes)
Creating a business plan, bank requirements for business plans
Knowing financing forms (equity, debt, and mezzanine financing)
Identifying financing sources (local bank, KfW, Crowdfunding, Venture Capital & Co.)
Accessing financing sources (Startup Pitch and Pitch Deck)
teaching_methods: Hybrid, seminar-based lecture with integrated exercises
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon passing the module exam. The grade's weighting for the final grade is determined by the credit points.
bibliography: KfW (Hrsg.): gruenderplattform.de und die Checklisten 1-6 zur Finanzplanung (Online)
